item.title: Anonymous But Not Really: The Hidden Ethics Problem in Your Course Survey
item.description:
Anonymous But Not Really: The Hidden Ethics Problem in Your Course Survey

“All answers and the survey itself will remain anonymous.”
— The survey you just logged into with your username and password.

Let that sink in for a moment.

You’ve been asked to evaluate a course. The system told you to log in. You typed your credentials. The platform recorded your session. And then — right there on the survey page — it promises you that everything is anonymous.

item.title: When the Algorithm Is Wrong: Understanding Bias and Fairness in AI
item.description:
When the Algorithm Is Wrong: Understanding Bias and Fairness in AI

“A system is only as fair as the values baked into it and most of us never get to see those values written down.”

I used to assume that algorithms were neutral. After all, they are just math, right? Numbers do not have opinions. Code does not discriminate. But the more I have studied AI ethics, the more I have come to understand that this assumption is not just wrong it is dangerous.
